The basic goal in any form of rummy is to build melds which can be either sets (three or four of a kind of the same rank) or runs (three or more sequential cards of the same suit) and either be first to go out or to amass more points than the opposition. This implementation includes 500 rummy (or 500 rum) and basic rummy, which are two of the most popular rummy games. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary One standard deck of 52 cards (without jokers) is used. Each player is dealt 13 cards in 2-player games or 7 cards in 3/4-player games. Draw At the start of each turn, a player may: Draw a card from the deck (cannot be undone as this reveals hidden information) Pick up the top card of the discard pile. The card cannot be discarded during the same turn. In 500 rummy ('splayed discard pile'), there is one more option: Pick up any lower card in the discard pile and all cards above that card together. The bottommost card the player took must be melded or be added to a meld immediately. If the deck has run out and the player does not want to draw a card from the discard pile, the player may end the round instead. Gameplay Players may perform any of these actions as many times as they want: Meld three or more consecutive cards of the same suit Meld three or four cards of the same rank Add (lay off) cards to a meld. The meld must be still valid after adding cards. Unless the player empties their hand by melding/adding (and going out), the player must end the turn by discarding a card to the discard pile. Discarding a card is not required to go out and end the round. Aces can be used as either high or low in 500 rummy ('versatile aces'), but in basic rummy ('low aces') aces are always low. In 'Meld/add restriction' option, melding is allowed only once per turn and adding cards to a meld is allowed only after playing at least one meld. Scoring The card scores are: 2 to 9: Face value (same as the number), or always 5 points in 'Simple scoring' option 10, Jack, Queen, King: 10 points Ace: In versatile aces, 15 points unless the ace is used as low (1 point). In low aces, always 1 point. In 'Simple scoring' option, low aces are 5 points instead of 1 point. In 500 rummy ('meld-hand scoring'), each player scores (the sum of card values melded/added) - (the sum of card values left in hand). In basic rummy ('positive scoring'), the round winner (who has the lowest hand value) scores the sum of card values in all other players' hands. If the round ends by the deck running out, the round winner's hand value is subtracted from each hand first. If tied the tied winners split the winning. In 'negative scoring' option, each player receives the penalty points equal to their hand value. The game ends when someone reaches the target score. [Rating: 1/10] This was one of my learning card games on the way to more interesting games such as cribbage and bridge.

[Rating: 1/10] It this day and age, with all these games, who on earth would ever choose to play this

[Rating: 2/10] Played this as a kid with the family (including grand parents). I guess it is okay for that, but actually it is not a good game.

[Rating: 2/10] Mind-numbing. It's one of the few games I could play with my family, but I never last more than a few rounds before losing myself daydreaming about any other game.

[Rating: 2.5/10] There are some decent Rummy variants, but I'm not a big fan of vanilla Rummy (500).

[Rating: 3/10] I used to love Rummy as a lad, then I discovered Gin and never played it again.  Now there are so many Euros that are rummy variants that I'm entirely sick of this system.

[Rating: 3/10] Seems really lame after you've played Canasta, Mahjong etc. Get Mystery Rummy instead.

[Rating: 3/10] Has never appealed to me even though I am a big card player. I have enjoyed an occasional rummy modification.

[Rating: 3/10] Usually play this with my mother who loves the game.  Many games I prefer to play, but it is quality time with my mother.

[Rating: 3/10] There's some choice to this one, but generally I like trick-taking games when all I have is a deck of cards.  500 rummy is probably my favorite, just because it's a lot of fun to pick up most of the discard pile in an effort to get more points out of it than you'll get stuck with.  You'll have to convince me to play this one, though.  I certainly won't suggest it.

[Rating: 3/10] Rummy is a good diversion, but with the many themed versions around, I would much rather play one of them. The Mystery Rummy series is quite excellent for starters.

[Rating: 3/10] Played a lot of this growing up, especially with the grandparents and my wife's family.

[Rating: 3/10] Nagyapámmal rengeteget játszottuk a '80-as években, ma már nem élvezném túlságosan szerintem.

[Rating: 3/10] The vanilla game isn't up to much - better to play Machiavelli (i.e. Rummikub) which makes a stressful jigsaw puzzle of the melding, or Gin Rummy which puts all the tension onto what players are hiding in their hands and how far they're going to push their luck.
